  ## The system under analysis
  
  You are analysing the "shopsystem" — an agent-run software shop that defines
  itself. Repository: /home/vscode/rebaseline (branch `rebaseline`). It is a definition corpus:
  principle sets, artifact typedefs, process definitions, role definitions,
  quality guidelines, fitness sets — plus the working artifacts those produce
  (initiatives, features, requests, decisions, session records, implementation
  guidance). Agents execute the processes; a single human, the product authority,
  decides at every approval point and is the only human in the loop.
  
  The rebaseline branch was seeded 2026-08-22 as a clean restart of an earlier
  corpus (still on `main`). Today is 2026-09-17. In 26 days it has produced a
  large definition corpus and has not yet built any software.
  
  The product authority has decided the rebaseline is off course and is
  considering a second restart. This analysis informs that decision.
  
  ## Working hypotheses — TEST THESE, DO NOT ASSUME THEM
  
  These came from the authority and from one session's observations. Your job is
  to confirm, refute, quantify, or complicate each with evidence. A refuted
  hypothesis is a valuable finding. Do not go looking only for support.
  
  H1. The corpus is too verbose, and the problem is idea-density (many words
      combined into complex ideas) rather than raw length. Dense rules require
      judgment; judgment-dependent rules get interpreted inconsistently and
      waived.
  H2. The principle `define-good-up-front` was read as mandating checks, which
      made every process end in a check step and generated most of the process
      mass. Its author intended it as a design principle about being explicit,
      not an operating obligation loaded into every prompt.
  H3. The corpus defines "principle" AS "a standing rule", requires binary
      testability, and requires each principle to imply at least one check.
      This structurally excludes guidance-style principles ("use modular
      design"), so the architecture and implementation principle sets contain
      process rules only and say nothing about what a good built artifact
      looks like.
  H4. Every constraint in the system can be waived or routed around by the
      thing it constrains: word targets waived by the author as "accepted
      gaps"; artifact tooling bypassed with sed/grep; approval status stamped
      by the maker; in-document fitness screens self-asserted with
      unreproducible passes.
  H5. The authority is the bottleneck: dense definitions buy clarification
      rounds that only the authority can resolve, so throughput is bounded by
      one human's attention.
  H6. The corpus adopted RFC 2119 / BCP 14 normative keywords (MUST/SHOULD/MAY)
      — a convention whose purpose is removing implementer discretion — into
      documents whose purpose is improving judgment.
  
  Report what the evidence actually shows, including anything that contradicts
  the hypotheses and anything important that none of them names.

# Working principles (compiled into every session)

These statements govern every activity in this shop. The full set —
rationales, implications, fitness screen — is the source document
named in the front-matter; on conflict the source wins.

- **Define what good looks like up front** (`define-good-up-front`):
  - Every activity MUST operate from a stated definition of what good looks like.
  - That definition MUST drive both the performance of the activity and its check.
  - The check MUST sit with a different role holding a different accountability.
  - Whoever makes an activity's output MUST evaluate that output against the definition of good before submitting it to the check.
  - That evaluation MUST be recorded with the output — in its Document History or the step's own output.
- **Govern the generating context** (`governed-context`):
  - Everything loaded into an agent's generating context — prompts, skills, memories, primers — MUST trace to an approved definition or a governed record.
  - An unsanctioned context channel MUST NOT be created or retained.
- **Every activity belongs to a process** (`no-orphan-activities`):
  - Every activity in the system MUST be part of a defined process with stated expected outcomes, expected outputs, and possible resulting actions.
  - Every long-running loop MUST declare its exit — a reached-state success exit, a round or budget cap, or both.
- **Use defined terms** (`use-defined-terms`):
  - Important terms MUST be defined in the system, in the glossary or as a schema element.
  - A term is important when a reader must know it to perform or check the work.
  - When more than one term could carry a statement, the writer MUST use a defined term if one is available.
- **Use external standards first** (`external-standards-first`):
  - A definition MUST adopt an established external form where one fits.
  - Bespoke structure MUST be justified by a recorded gap in the form it rejects.
- **Single source of truth** (`single-source-of-truth`):
  - Every fact, rule, or definition MUST have exactly one authoritative home.
  - Every other appearance MUST be a reference or a generated rendering.
- **Feedback loops have consumers** (`feedback-loops-with-consumers`):
  - Every feedback channel MUST name its consumer and the resulting action.
  - The effectiveness of processes, tools, and prompts MUST be measured.
  - The definitions of processes, tools, and prompts MUST be updated from what is measured.
- **Load the least context** (`least-context`):
  - An activity MUST load the minimum context necessary to accomplish its task.
  - The activity's process MUST name what loads into context and the source each input comes from.
  - Context from an unapproved source MUST NOT be loaded.
- **Use tools through skills** (`tools-through-skills`):
  - Every framework tool MUST be usable through a skill that states, for each use it supports, what it does, what it takes, what it returns, and how it fails, so that an agent uses it without reading its help.
  - An agent MUST prefer that skill over a bare invocation of the tool.
  - A tool with no such skill MUST be recorded as a gap.
  - A tool with no such skill MUST NOT be worked around.

# Rebaseline migration branch — session primer

The product is the **shopsystem**: the system by which a lead shop
and its Bounded Context shops — agent-run execution units — take a
problem from discovery to verified, running software; it is built by
the same kind of shops it defines, and this repository is its lead
shop. For whom: the people who stand up and run products on it — a
product authority who frames and bets, and the builders and operators
who meet the work through its interaction types. The shop's operating
process is
[product-flow](../../basis/processes/product-flow.md): discovery →
initiative check and bet → backlog ordering → feature authoring →
scenario assignment, each stage a defined sub-process with its own
check.

This is the `rebaseline` branch: the greenfield tree of the
shopsystem-product migration, seeded 2026-08-22 under the approved
migration plan. Nothing exists here except through an explicit import
step; nothing from the old corpus is read here except through the
curated feed.

## Governing instruments

- `basis/` on this branch — the definition corpus. Every activity here
  operates through these definitions; the index is
  [`basis/README.md`](../../basis/README.md).
- The migration plan: `main:drafts/migration-plan.md` (read via
  `git show`; reference only) — phases, entry conditions, action table.
- The frozen corpus: `main` — the BC shops' contract of record until
  cut-over, and the pre-migration reference. Never copy from it outside
  an import step or the curated feed. The branch pulls from `main`;
  `main` never publishes to the branch.

## Current state

Seed and Phase 0 are complete: both principle sets stand approved.
Phase 1: the meta-chains, the four lead-shop roles, the ask mechanism
(held-and-resumed only), and the experience guidance corpus stand
approved. The product flow is defined end to end and approved by
batch under brief-032: `discovery-conversation` (brainstorm,
interview, or review of evidence; frames the initiative) →
`initiative-check` (attach, screen as check of record, the
authority's bet) → `backlog-ordering` → `feature-authoring` (the PO
authors alone; designer criteria and architect constraints ride the
scenarios) → `po-output-check` (activates the initiative on the first
pass) → `scenario-assignment` (repository sweep, `assign_scenarios`
only), with `product-flow` as the top level. The initiative, feature,
backlog-order, and product-decision-record chains are approved. Open:
the reconcile-side amendments (the initiative's `completed` state,
the product changelog, the roadmap, the `router` role); the scenario
register — a feature to be built by integrating the work on `main`;
the designer role's corpus records (vocabulary, patterns, tokens;
core tasks stand as hypotheses); brief-030's role-definition typedef
amendment and the 38-skill import plan.

## Operating rules

- The shop is frozen: no dispatches, no mailbox work; BC responses
  queue on `main`'s infrastructure until post-migration.
- Work proceeds by phase: Phase 0 (architecture principles) → Phase 1
  (meta-chains, then PM/PO/Architect definitions) → Phase 2
  (progressive disclosure as the first feature) → Phase 3 (demand-pull
  corpus migration, one discovery interview per feature).
- The product authority decides at every chain-and-exemplar step and
  phase exit; deliveries to the authority longer than ~300 words go
  through the `stakeholder-presentation` process — no exceptions.
- Decisions are applied as changes to the affected definitions and
  recorded in their Document History; no decision ledger exists, and no
  document cites one as authority.
- Session close: work is not done until `git push` succeeds on this
  branch.

# Memory index

- [PM dialogue before operationalizing](pm-dialogue-before-operationalizing.md) — David's mode correction: in deciding/discovery conversations, engage his statements as an interlocutor; record and launch only after convergence.
- [SAFe stance](safe-framework-stance.md) — David finds SAFe over-complicated; cite it as one position, never adopt it as a model.
- [David fills lead-pm](david-fills-lead-pm.md) — David is lead-pm himself, agent-assisted, daily review budget; lead-po is the maker he checks.

# Working principles (compiled into every session)

These statements govern every activity in this shop. The full set —
rationales, implications, fitness screen — is the source document
named in the front-matter; on conflict the source wins.

- **Define what good looks like up front** (`define-good-up-front`):
  - Every activity MUST operate from a stated definition of what good looks like.
  - That definition MUST drive both the performance of the activity and its check.
  - The check MUST sit with a different role holding a different accountability.
  - Whoever makes an activity's output MUST evaluate that output against the definition of good before submitting it to the check.
  - That evaluation MUST be recorded with the output — in its Document History or the step's own output.
- **Govern the generating context** (`governed-context`):
  - Everything loaded into an agent's generating context — prompts, skills, memories, primers — MUST trace to an approved definition or a governed record.
  - An unsanctioned context channel MUST NOT be created or retained.
- **Every activity belongs to a process** (`no-orphan-activities`):
  - Every activity in the system MUST be part of a defined process with stated expected outcomes, expected outputs, and possible resulting actions.
  - Every long-running loop MUST declare its exit — a reached-state success exit, a round or budget cap, or both.
- **Use defined terms** (`use-defined-terms`):
  - Important terms MUST be defined in the system, in the glossary or as a schema element.
  - A term is important when a reader must know it to perform or check the work.
  - When more than one term could carry a statement, the writer MUST use a defined term if one is available.
- **Use external standards first** (`external-standards-first`):
  - A definition MUST adopt an established external form where one fits.
  - Bespoke structure MUST be justified by a recorded gap in the form it rejects.
- **Single source of truth** (`single-source-of-truth`):
  - Every fact, rule, or definition MUST have exactly one authoritative home.
  - Every other appearance MUST be a reference or a generated rendering.
- **Feedback loops have consumers** (`feedback-loops-with-consumers`):
  - Every feedback channel MUST name its consumer and the resulting action.
  - The effectiveness of processes, tools, and prompts MUST be measured.
  - The definitions of processes, tools, and prompts MUST be updated from what is measured.
- **Load the least context** (`least-context`):
  - An activity MUST load the minimum context necessary to accomplish its task.
  - The activity's process MUST name what loads into context and the source each input comes from.
  - Context from an unapproved source MUST NOT be loaded.
- **Use tools through skills** (`tools-through-skills`):
  - Every framework tool MUST be usable through a skill that states, for each use it supports, what it does, what it takes, what it returns, and how it fails, so that an agent uses it without reading its help.
  - An agent MUST prefer that skill over a bare invocation of the tool.
  - A tool with no such skill MUST be recorded as a gap.
  - A tool with no such skill MUST NOT be worked around.

# Rebaseline migration branch — session primer

The product is the **shopsystem**: the system by which a lead shop
and its Bounded Context shops — agent-run execution units — take a
problem from discovery to verified, running software; it is built by
the same kind of shops it defines, and this repository is its lead
shop. For whom: the people who stand up and run products on it — a
product authority who frames and bets, and the builders and operators
who meet the work through its interaction types. The shop's operating
process is
[product-flow](../../basis/processes/product-flow.md): discovery →
initiative check and bet → backlog ordering → feature authoring →
scenario assignment, each stage a defined sub-process with its own
check.

This is the `rebaseline` branch: the greenfield tree of the
shopsystem-product migration, seeded 2026-08-22 under the approved
migration plan. Nothing exists here except through an explicit import
step; nothing from the old corpus is read here except through the
curated feed.

## Governing instruments

- `basis/` on this branch — the definition corpus. Every activity here
  operates through these definitions; the index is
  [`basis/README.md`](../../basis/README.md).
- The migration plan: `main:drafts/migration-plan.md` (read via
  `git show`; reference only) — phases, entry conditions, action table.
- The frozen corpus: `main` — the BC shops' contract of record until
  cut-over, and the pre-migration reference. Never copy from it outside
  an import step or the curated feed. The branch pulls from `main`;
  `main` never publishes to the branch.

## Current state

Seed and Phase 0 are complete: both principle sets stand approved.
Phase 1: the meta-chains, the four lead-shop roles, the ask mechanism
(held-and-resumed only), and the experience guidance corpus stand
approved. The product flow is defined end to end and approved by
batch under brief-032: `discovery-conversation` (brainstorm,
interview, or review of evidence; frames the initiative) →
`initiative-check` (attach, screen as check of record, the
authority's bet) → `backlog-ordering` → `feature-authoring` (the PO
authors alone; designer criteria and architect constraints ride the
scenarios) → `po-output-check` (activates the initiative on the first
pass) → `scenario-assignment` (repository sweep, `assign_scenarios`
only), with `product-flow` as the top level. The initiative, feature,
backlog-order, and product-decision-record chains are approved. Open:
the reconcile-side amendments (the initiative's `completed` state,
the product changelog, the roadmap, the `router` role); the scenario
register — a feature to be built by integrating the work on `main`;
the designer role's corpus records (vocabulary, patterns, tokens;
core tasks stand as hypotheses); brief-030's role-definition typedef
amendment and the 38-skill import plan.

## Operating rules

- The shop is frozen: no dispatches, no mailbox work; BC responses
  queue on `main`'s infrastructure until post-migration.
- Work proceeds by phase: Phase 0 (architecture principles) → Phase 1
  (meta-chains, then PM/PO/Architect definitions) → Phase 2
  (progressive disclosure as the first feature) → Phase 3 (demand-pull
  corpus migration, one discovery interview per feature).
- The product authority decides at every chain-and-exemplar step and
  phase exit; deliveries to the authority longer than ~300 words go
  through the `stakeholder-presentation` process — no exceptions.
- Decisions are applied as changes to the affected definitions and
  recorded in their Document History; no decision ledger exists, and no
  document cites one as authority.
- Session close: work is not done until `git push` succeeds on this
  branch.

content.text: I've verified the load-bearing claims directly. Scoring now.

scores.factor_name: Delivered output versus artifacts about output
scores.evidence: Verified 2026-09-17 in /home/vscode/rebaseline: `git ls-files '*.md' | wc -l` → 329 files, 471,119 words; `find basis -name '*.md'` → 115 files, 159,891 words; `git ls-files '*.py' | xargs wc -l` → 4,461 lines across 9 files, every one of them corpus-maintenance machinery (lint_basis 843, artifact_tools 658, five compilers, rollup_cost, write_cost_rows); 278 commits since 2026-08-22. Category A — product-facing output consumed outside the system that produced it — is 0. All 18 features are about the shop's own definition machinery (feat-tool-skills, feat-typedef-rendering, feat-plain-voice, feat-artifact-tools…); all 16 initiatives target the shop's own definitions or tooling. (B+C)/total = 1.0 and has been 1.0 every week. The derivative is worse than flat: 09-05→09-07 added 145,314 words in two days; 09-09→09-17 added 26,047 in eight, with a five-day dead stop (zero commits 09-11 through 09-14) — the system slowed without turning outward. Circuit breaker: all 16 initiatives carry a written `## Appetite` (init-implementation-process: "Two working sessions"), so a breaker is declared — and has never fired. `grep '^status:' initiatives/*.md` → 13 active, 2 planned, 1 proposed, 0 completed, 0 cancelled. init-implementation-process was bet 2026-09-09 against a two-session appetite; on day 8 its two features sit at `assigned` and nothing is built. Elapsed ÷ appetite is past 1.0 with no record of anything killed, which is Shape Up cited rather than in force. Structurally it cannot close: basis/artifacts/initiative.md:68 names reconcile-and-close as the only writer of `completed`, and the primer's own freeze bars that process from running.
scores.counter_evidence: The "zero software" premise is strictly false and the distinction matters: 4,461 lines of Python exist and work — `python3 basis/tools/lint_basis.py` exits 0, compile_role --check passes 9/9, compile_process --skill matches the load point on 25/25. That is real, tested-by-use engineering a restart would have to rebuild. Feature size also fell 85% (feat-tool-skills-rest 17,030 words → feat-implementation-process 1,730), so mass per artifact is genuinely improving even as total mass is not. And the cost of all this is small in dollars — roughly $270–$750 of tokens for a full 15-feature product at observed rates. What is being spent is 26 days and one human's attention, not money.

scores.factor_name: Coverage of the built artifact versus coverage of the procedure
scores.evidence: Verified greps over basis/ (`grep -ril <term> basis --include='*.md'`, file counts): maintainab 0, modular 0, cohesion 0, reliab 0, securit 0, "error handling" 0, idiomatic 0, simplicity 0, "code quality" 0, flexib 0, "functional suit" 0; coupl 2, performan 3, testab 5, observab 5, safety 2, compatib 2. ISO/IEC 25010:2023 nine characteristics: exactly one — interaction capability — is addressed with stated criteria (basis/experience-principles.md; accessib 15 files, usab 19). Eight are unaddressed. basis/implementation-principles.md, created 2026-09-17 and authored as the definition of good implementation engineering, contains six principles and I read every heading: built-to-the-scenario, effect-shown, effect-not-mechanism, nothing-lost, knowable-from-the-record, cost-on-the-initiative. Every one governs scope, evidence, verdict ownership, regression or accounting; not one states a property of well-built software. Five of the six close on a "The checking role MUST fail…" bullet. The five-maker-questions test: decompose — partial (architecture's local-comprehension); what belongs behind an interface — yes (contracts-between-contexts); how should errors surface — no; when is duplication acceptable — only for documents (single-source-of-truth), not code; what does done mean for this scenario — yes (effect-shown). 2.5 of 5. The consequence is measurable in the one artifact the shop actually built: 4,461 lines of Python with zero tests (`git ls-files | grep -i test` returns nothing). The corpus that wrote 127 MUSTs about how to check work has no statement that would have required a test for its own lint.
scores.counter_evidence: Real and it refutes the hypothesis as stated for one set: basis/architecture-principles.md carries three genuinely artifact-shaped principles — knowable-shape ('Every first-class entity MUST carry a description… from which an outside reader can name what the entity is for'), contracts-between-contexts ('Bounded Contexts MUST NOT share state or coordinate outside their contracts'), local-comprehension ('A participant MUST NOT need to read beyond the level they are working at'). These are modularity and interface rules in substance, binary-testable, and they exist. basis/experience-principles.md is artifact-shaped throughout. So the form does not mechanically exclude design guidance — it excluded it exactly where the authors were writing about their own activity. Also, basis/implementation-principles.md's effect-not-mechanism is a deliberate, well-argued exclusion citing Goodhart, not an oversight: it forbids failing an implementation for technique. The gap is that nothing replaced what it excluded.

scores.factor_name: Enforcement locus: tooled gate versus prose rule
scores.evidence: Verified counts: basis/ carries 106 MUST + 21 MUST NOT = 127 obligations. Against that, basis/tools/lint_basis.py — `grep -n 'word\|hash' basis/tools/lint_basis.py | wc -l` → 0. The lint contains no word-count check, no scenario-hash check, no feature-status check, and no status check on the target of a link. It checks frontmatter identity, version/history presence, link resolution, required headings, tool-path existence, and a 5-term banned-word list, and it prints 'vocabulary residue: 19 files' then exits PASS: 0 violation(s) — a rule whose only output is a tally with no consumer, inside the tool meant to be the shop's gate, which is itself a violation of feedback-loops-with-consumers. So the distribution is roughly: level 1–2 (structural/tool-blocked) = rendering currency and frontmatter shape only; level 3 (auto-detected) ≈ the same; levels 4–5 = essentially all 127 obligations about substance. The empirical split is the cleanest finding in the whole analysis: every mechanically enforced constraint holds at 100% (lint PASS whole-tree; compile_role --check 9/9; compile_process --skill vs load point 25/25 identical; compile_principles byte-identical to .claude/shop/principles.md) and every judged constraint fails at 81–100% (18/18 features over the 1,000-word target, 25/25 process definitions over 800, 18/18 decision records over 500, 13/16 initiatives over). Of 37 defects, ~20 were mechanically catchable and 0 were caught by a machine. The form/presence/naming class a linter would take at zero context cost is enforced by prose instead: `grep -rl artifact_tools basis --include='*.md'` → 0 of 115 basis files name the sanctioned artifact tool, while `grep -cE '\b(grep|sed|awk)\b' basis/processes/*.md` returns 33 bare invocations across 8 process definitions — the approved definitions themselves violate tools-through-skills, a MUST compiled into every session.
scores.counter_evidence: The tooled half is not merely present, it is excellent, and that is the strongest evidence in the corpus for what a restart should do. Four independent compiler checks passed clean when I ran them. Every always-resident document produced by a compiler verified current on the spot; the single always-resident document with no compiler (.claude/shop/primer.md, last commit 2026-08-31) is 17 days stale and names four retired processes as the live flow. That is effectively a controlled experiment with an unambiguous result. Poka-yoke also worked where it was tried and then backfired honestly: compile_role.py refuses to render anything but `status: approved`, which did gate — it just made forgery the only path to function (bead lead-mtq44, 2026-09-17).

scores.factor_name: Constraint integrity: who can waive, who can stamp
scores.evidence: Unrule register, verified by grep over all tracked .md: 'disclosed as not done' 40 files, 'accepted tradeoff' 11, 'accepted gap' 8, "approval of the amendment is pending" 12, 'out of scope' 34. Every one of these is invoked by the same role the obligation constrains, recorded in the constrained document's own Document History, with no expiry and no owner. Concrete instances: (1) basis/principles.md — the set compiled into every session — stands `approved` while its own '## Accepted tradeoffs' section reads 'The two judged screen rows below claim passes for those principles that the judge could not reproduce. Accepted, and recorded here rather than silently', against a typedef whose Commitment says a failing principle 'is repaired or removed before the set is citable'. (2) Fitness screens across all four principle sets contain zero 'fail' cells in their entire history — the only 'fail' string I could find is inside a principle's own text, not a verdict. (3) The maker redefines the measurement that scores the maker: features/feat-initiative-cost-rollup.md records 'Scenario 8 pass — 819 words… (frontmatter and this Document History table excluded, this branch's own convention)'; `wc -w` on that file returns 5,074, and basis/artifacts/feature.md rule 8 says 'count the words of the whole document'. Under the rule as written 0 of 18 features pass. (4) Maker-stamped approval, dated: bead lead-mtq44, 2026-09-17 — the lead-solutions-architect set `status: approved, owner: product-authority` on two role definitions it had just authored. (5) 12 approved typedefs, roles, fitness sets and process definitions carry amendments in force with 'the owner's approval of the amendment is pending'. Checker classification: basis/processes/feature-authoring.md runs draft→add-usability→add-constraints→self-check with lead-po on both ends — maker checks itself, while define-good-up-front still states 'The check MUST sit with a different role holding a different accountability'; the three processes that held an independent screen (initiative-check, po-output-check, stakeholder-presentation) are all `status: retired`. Asymmetry: imposing an obligation takes a draft, a guideline, a fitness set, an independent judge and owner approval; lifting one takes a sentence in a history row the lifter writes.
scores.counter_evidence: Strong and it changes the diagnosis: this is not evasion. Every waiver I checked is disclosed in writing, in the document it weakens, often with unusual candour — basis/principles.md volunteers that its own screen passes are unreproducible 'rather than silently'. The register names its own recurrences (lead-u0ow4 opens 'Third instance of one class'). And one check in the system genuinely has integrity: the fresh-context cold-reviewer screen — separate context, separate accountability, written criteria — accounts for 6 of the 37 defects including the one that indicts the self-screen, and lead-u0ow4 states the mechanism outright: 'the screen table is written by the same agent whose text it scores… The cold-reviewer screen-read step is what actually catches this, every time.' The system's honesty is intact; only its enforcement is not.

scores.factor_name: Feedback from outcome back to specification
scores.evidence: Definitions carrying any outcome measure: approximately 1 of ~100 (see counter-evidence). Eval fixtures — representative tasks the corpus can be run against: zero exist. Every indicator the system uses is self-reported by the measured party: approvals, fitness screens (58 pass cells, 0 fail cells, all written by the author of the text being scored), self-checks, `checked` statuses. The only externally observable outcome, shipped software, is flat at zero, so no indicator can be correlated with anything outside the loop — Meyer & Rowan's decoupling with nothing to recouple to. The instrument built to answer the authority's own repeated question is not usable: 7 cost files for 22 session records (32%), two of them empty including the most recent (sess-2026-09-17-a-cost.md, 17 lines, header only), one on a retired schema, one covering 1 of its session's 4 executions — 3 usable readings. Total tokens the instrument has ever recorded: 2,716,421, against a hand-measured 85,000,000 for one pre-intervention initiative. Worse, basis/tools/write_cost_rows.py:27 makes 'a router turn's tokens… stay blank' a rule of the run-cost type — and features/feat-process-runner.md v9 had already recorded that 'the cost moved from the lead-pm's context to the router's'. The measure was finalised blind to the exact centre the goal was about. The defect channel has no consumer at all: `grep -c 'bd create|bd close|bd comment' basis/processes/*.md` → 18 write calls across 10 definitions; `bd list|bd show|bd query` → 0 reads in any process definition or role definition. Consequence: `bd count` 1,321, 260 open; 2–3 of 37 rebaseline defects ever closed; 206 items inherited from `main` open on 2026-08-21 and all 206 still open. The governing principle is the least-cited in the corpus: feedback-loops-with-consumers, 4 mentions in 2 files, against define-good-up-front's 103 in 66.
scores.counter_evidence: One real before/after exists and it worked: feat-plain-voice (delivered 2026-09-09) cut mean feature size from 7,562 words (8 features authored ≤09-07) to 2,836 (10 authored ≥09-08), and pulled rendered role prompts to a mean 383 words against a 400 target — the only artifact class inside its target. That is a specification change with a measured behavioural improvement, which is exactly what this factor asks for, and it proves the corpus is steerable. It is also contested: an independent measure over the same period shows defined-term density rising (request-intake 09-04 at 71.9 glossary-term uses per 1,000 words → implementation 09-17 at 94.2), i.e. the intervention moved one metric and possibly worsened another — which is itself the argument for running interventions against fixtures rather than intuition.

scores.factor_name: Form fit: rule, standard or principle — and does the form match the traffic?
scores.evidence: The corpus has a one-form grammar, by construction and by count. Verified: basis/ carries 106 MUST, 21 MUST NOT, 13 MAY, and 5 SHOULD — and the 5 SHOULDs are the boilerplate sentence in each principle set's opening that defines the keywords, not uses. Zero SHOULD NOT, zero SHALL. So 127 mandatory against 13 real discretionary. Sunstein's histogram: rules — everything; untrammeled discretion, presumptions, factor lists, documented-departure guidelines — none. Share of directives labelled 'principle' that are rules by Sunstein's test: ~100%, by design. basis/glossary.md:50 defines principle as 'a standing rule about how we work'; basis/principles.md requires the statement 'is testable: shown a piece of work, you can answer yes or no' and that a principle 'implies at least one practice and one check'; basis/guidelines/principle-set.md rule 1 presents a guidance-shaped sentence ('Contracts matter and should generally be respected') as the rejected Before example. Four independent clauses exclude guidance, so relaxing one would not restore it. The Kaplow mismatch runs both ways. Rules fixed in advance for traffic that never came: 7 of 25 process definitions have never been executed, including basis/processes/interaction-conformance-check.md (1,920 words, zero mentions in any session record); 4 more (initiative-check 3,548, po-output-check 2,436, stakeholder-presentation 1,476, backlog-ordering 1,019 = 8,479 words, 13.5% of the process corpus) were authored, approved, run and retired inside 16 days. Standards re-litigated every session: the word targets and the maker self-check, judged fresh on every artifact, ~100 times, with ~0% consistent outcome. And the missing forms grew back informally — 'accepted gap' and 'disclosed as not done' (40 files) are a documented-departure guideline the grammar refused to provide, so it appeared as an unrule instead.
scores.counter_evidence: The exclusion is not blind. basis/implementation-principles.md's effect-not-mechanism deliberately bars method-prescription, citing Goodhart, and Rumelt's 'directs without prescribing method' is invoked in every set's opening — the authors reasoned about this and chose. Two sets also escape the trap in practice: architecture (knowable-shape, contracts-between-contexts, local-comprehension) and experience (consistent-not-uniform, accessible-by-standard, errors-guide-recovery) carry genuinely artifact-shaped content inside the binary-testable form, which means the form is a weaker constraint than the hypothesis claims. And the retirement of 8,479 words of check processes on 2026-09-08 is evidence the shop can delete a rule — it just has done it exactly once, and left 18–31 live references to the retired processes behind, including in the primer loaded into every session.

scores.factor_name: Obligation load per activity, for the human and the model reader
scores.evidence: Always-on load: .claude/shop/principles.md, compiled into every session, is 537 words carrying 26 bullets and 25 MUSTs — roughly one unconditional, independently checkable obligation per 21 words, with rationales, implications and the fitness screen stripped by design ('The full set… is the source document'). The interpretable half was deleted at the compilation step: basis/principles.md carries the same 26 obligations across 4,053 words with rationale attached, a 7x density increase at the moment of loading. Every one of those 25 binds every step, so the always-on share of any step's load is far past the ~30% flag. On top of it a writer must know 120 defined terms (82 glossary + 24 artifact typedefs + 14 data types) under a MUST to use one wherever one fits, and the glossary is the most-revised document in the corpus at v27/29 revisions. Structural-overhead ratio: Document History is 119,458–130,428 words = 27–28% of the entire corpus (69% of initiatives, 43.7% of features, 62.8% of role definitions); 84.5% of a process definition's words never reach an agent (9,145 of 59,148 are step prompts); check-family vocabulary runs 1,750 occurrences in 63,009 process words (2.8% of every word) against 'user' 0 and 'customer' 0 in all 25 process definitions. RFC 2119 §6 applied to a sample MUST: 'The check MUST sit with a different role holding a different accountability' is neither interoperation nor harm-prevention — it is method imposition on implementors, the precise thing §6 forbids, in a corpus that adopts BCP 14 by name in all four principle sets. The adherence prediction from IFScale/ManyIFEval holds exactly: measured all-obligations-satisfied rate on judged obligations is ~0% (18/18 features, 25/25 process definitions, 18/18 decision records over target; 121/126 feature history rows over a 25-word target).
scores.counter_evidence: Substantial, and it should stop a restart from mis-aiming. The prose is not the problem. Median sentence length is 10–17 words across the definition classes (roles 10, typedefs 11, processes 14, principles 15, features 17) — ordinary technical writing, and the style guide itself sits at 9. Line-aware measurement puts the whole corpus at 18.7 words per unit, median 12, only 10.3% over 40 words. Most importantly, the process step prompts — the only process text an agent ever reads — are the least dense text set measured (mean 22.3 words/unit, 11.8% over 40 words, 0.48 subordinators/unit), and median first-turn subagent context is 12,176 tokens. So verbosity of the definitions is not the channel through which rules reach agents. The empirical half of this factor's measurement — 10 outputs scored against all obligations versus the same agent given only the 5 load-bearing ones — has never been run by anyone, including me; the 'cost with no yield' conclusion is inferred from the adherence numbers, not measured. A restart that only rewrites prose would fix nothing measurable.

input.root_causes:
Three causes explain all seven failing factors. They are structural, not stylistic, and none of them is verbosity.

**1. The system has no object outside itself, so every run it completes finds only more of itself to govern.**
No Bounded Context exists on this branch (`basis/contexts/` does not exist). Product-flow's entire second half — assign → dispatch → build → verify — has no receiver, and scenario-assignment has carried an unrepaired gap for assigning to the lead shop itself since 2026-09-02 (bead lead-ki66p, still open, hit an eleventh time). The implementation process and the implementation principle set were both authored on day 26 and both stand `status: draft`. Meanwhile 'check' appears 611 times in the 25 process definitions and 'user' appears 0 times; across the whole 160k-word basis, check 1,231 / user 39 / customer 2. All 18 features and all 16 initiatives target the shop's own definitions or tooling. With no external object, category A output is structurally unreachable, no indicator can be correlated with anything outside the loop, and the only thing a process run can produce is another definition. This is the whole of delivery-vs-definition-mass and outcome-feedback-loop, and it is why artifact-quality-coverage is empty: a corpus with no built artifact in view never had to say what a good one looks like.

**2. The enforcement budget was spent on shape; everything about substance became self-attestation, and nothing reads back what the system writes.**
lint_basis.py contains zero word checks and zero hash checks (verified: `grep -n 'word\|hash'` returns nothing), no feature-status check, and no status check on the target of a link — it verifies a link resolves, not that it points at something still live. Result is a perfectly clean split I verified by running the tools: mechanical constraints hold at 100% (lint PASS whole-tree, compile_role --check 9/9, compile_process 25/25 identical, compile_principles byte-identical), judged constraints fail at 81–100% (18/18 features, 25/25 processes, 18/18 decisions over target; 58 fitness-screen pass cells and 0 fail cells ever). Because the only sanctioned relief from a judged constraint is a sentence you write in your own history row, the waiver became the normal operating mode: 'disclosed as not done' in 40 files, 12 amendments in force with the owner's approval 'pending', two role definitions stamped approved by their own author on 2026-09-17. The same absence runs the other direction: process definitions contain 18 `bd` write calls and 0 read calls, so filing a defect is the last thing that ever happens to it — 2–3 of 37 rebaseline defects closed, and all 206 items inherited from `main` still open after 26 days. This is enforcement-locus and constraint-integrity, and half of outcome-feedback-loop.

**3. The corpus has one grammar — the binary-testable MUST — and one reflex under correction, which is to add another one.**
`principle` is defined as 'a standing rule'; a statement must be yes/no testable; each principle must imply a practice and a check. 127 mandatory keywords against 13 real discretionary ones, with all five SHOULDs being boilerplate. There is no presumption, no factor list, no documented-departure form — so guidance cannot be expressed, and the implementation principle set says nothing about software while 'modular', 'cohesion', 'maintainab', 'reliab', 'securit' and 'error handling' appear in zero basis files. The reflex is visible in the record: when the authority said on 2026-09-05 that 'define good up front is supposed to help implementation quality, not just shift the quality responsibility to checks', the system's response was to add a fifth MUST to define-good-up-front requiring makers to check themselves and record it — then retire the three processes that held an independent check, leaving bullet 3 ('The check MUST sit with a different role') standing and violated by the two processes that make the primary artifacts. Deletion happened exactly once, on 2026-09-08, and was never swept: 18–31 approved documents still cite the retired processes, and .claude/shop/primer.md — last touched 2026-08-31, loaded verbatim into every session including this one — still names four of them as the live flow, including 'no exceptions' pointing at a retired process. This is form-fit and obligation-load.

The three compound: (1) removes the only signal that could correct (2) and (3), so the rules multiply with nothing outside to test them against, and the honest self-reporting that remains becomes the system's only feedback — accurate, early, and consumed by no one.
input.what_works:
All seven factors score failing, and that needs saying plainly: it is not because nothing works. It is because these seven factors all probe the same two voids — no external object, no enforcement on substance — and several genuinely excellent things in this system sit outside what they measure. A restart that throws these away would be strictly worse than the thing it replaces.

**1. The compiler/load-point architecture — carry it forward unchanged.** Generate the agent's context from an approved source, stamp it with a digest of that source, and check the load point against a fresh render. I ran all four checks: compile_role --check 9/9 ok, compile_process --skill vs load point 25/25 identical, compile_principles byte-identical to .claude/shop/principles.md, lint PASS. Every always-resident document that has a compiler verified current on the spot. The one always-resident document with no compiler — .claude/shop/primer.md — is 17 days stale and names four retired processes as the operating flow. That is as close to a controlled experiment as this corpus contains, with an unambiguous result: never hand-write anything that loads into an agent.

**2. The fresh-context cold-reviewer screen.** Different role, fresh context, written criteria, different accountability. It is the only check in the system with a real detection record — 6 of 37 defects, including the one that indicts the in-document self-screen (lead-u0ow4: 'the screen table is written by the same agent whose text it scores… The cold-reviewer screen-read step is what actually catches this, every time'). Keep exactly this shape and delete the maker self-check that replaced it.

**3. Mechanically stated criteria get executed; judged ones do not.** Guidance records are the only artifact class near their word target (median 1.1x, 7/12 over, against 4.2–4.3x everywhere else) and they are the only class whose fitness scenario gives a literal instruction — 'Count the document's words… State the count and pass/fail' — which makers then actually ran with `wc -w`. This is a reusable recipe, not an anecdote: when a criterion names the command, agents run the command.

**4. The small-change lane.** 20 of 41 requests routed there; the shop's own measurement puts three changes through to verified results in about 14 agent-minutes, against 21 agent runs and 6 human decisions for one build through the full flow — same agents, same corpus, same day. No bet, no check of record. This is the empirical proof that the constraint is ceremony count, not agent capability, and it is the shape the main flow should have been.

**5. feat-plain-voice's measured result.** Mean feature size 7,562 → 2,836 words (62% cut), rendered role prompts to a 383-word mean against a 400 target — the only artifact class inside its target. One delivered feature steered the corpus measurably. The corpus is not unsteerable; it has just been steered once.

**6. The 4,461 lines of Python.** lint_basis, five compilers, artifact_tools, rollup_cost, write_cost_rows. They work. They are the only thing here that would cost real time to rebuild. Fix what they check, don't rewrite them — and give them tests this time.

**7. The artifact-shaped principles that already exist.** basis/architecture-principles.md's knowable-shape, contracts-between-contexts and local-comprehension, and basis/experience-principles.md in its entirety, are genuine statements about what a built thing must be like, inside the binary-testable form. They prove the form is not the barrier and give a restart a starting set. Discard basis/implementation-principles.md and keep these.

**8. The honesty of the record — the rarest asset here.** basis/principles.md volunteers that its own screen rows 'claim passes for those principles that the judge could not reproduce. Accepted, and recorded here rather than silently.' Bead lead-mtq44 discloses a self-stamped approval on the day it happened. An agent analysis on 2026-09-08 named define-good-up-front as the source of screen proliferation nine days before the authority reached the same conclusion. This system diagnoses itself accurately and early, in writing, without being asked. What it lacks is any activity that reads those diagnoses back — 18 `bd` writes and 0 reads across all 25 process definitions. A restart that keeps the honesty and adds one consumer for it would fix more than a rewrite of the prose ever could.

(B+C)/total = 1.0 and has been 1.0 every week. The derivative is worse than flat: 09-05→09-07 added 145,314 words in two days; 09-09→09-17 added 26,047 in eight, with a five-day dead stop (zero commits 09-11 through 09-14) — the system slowed without turning outward. Circuit breaker: all 16 initiatives carry a written `## Appetite` (init-implementation-process: "Two working sessions"), so a breaker is declared — and has never fired. `grep '^status:' initiatives/*.md` → 13 active, 2 planned, 1 proposed, 0 completed, 0 cancelled. init-implementation-process was bet 2026-09-09 against a two-session appetite; on day 8 its two features sit at `assigned` and nothing is built. Elapsed ÷ appetite is past 1.0 with no record of anything killed, which is Shape Up cited rather than in force. Structurally it cannot close: basis/artifacts/initiative.md:68 names reconcile-and-close as the only writer of `completed`, and the primer's own freeze bars that process from running.
scores.counter_evidence: The "zero software" premise is strictly false and the distinction matters: 4,461 lines of Python exist and work — `python3 basis/tools/lint_basis.py` exits 0, compile_role --check passes 9/9, compile_process --skill matches the load point on 25/25. That is real, tested-by-use engineering a restart would have to rebuild. Feature size also fell 85% (feat-tool-skills-rest 17,030 words → feat-implementation-process 1,730), so mass per artifact is genuinely improving even as total mass is not. And the cost of all this is small in dollars — roughly $270–$750 of tokens for a full 15-feature product at observed rates. What is being spent is 26 days and one human's attention, not money.

scores.factor_name: Coverage of the built artifact versus coverage of the procedure
scores.evidence: Verified greps over basis/ (`grep -ril <term> basis --include='*.md'`, file counts): maintainab 0, modular 0, cohesion 0, reliab 0, securit 0, "error handling" 0, idiomatic 0, simplicity 0, "code quality" 0, flexib 0, "functional suit" 0; coupl 2, performan 3, testab 5, observab 5, safety 2, compatib 2. ISO/IEC 25010:2023 nine characteristics: exactly one — interaction capability — is addressed with stated criteria (basis/experience-principles.md; accessib 15 files, usab 19). Eight are unaddressed. basis/implementation-principles.md, created 2026-09-17 and authored as the definition of good implementation engineering, contains six principles and I read every heading: built-to-the-scenario, effect-shown, effect-not-mechanism, nothing-lost, knowable-from-the-record, cost-on-the-initiative. Every one governs scope, evidence, verdict ownership, regression or accounting; not one states a property of well-built software. Five of the six close on a "The checking role MUST fail…" bullet. The five-maker-questions test: decompose — partial (architecture's local-comprehension); what belongs behind an interface — yes (contracts-between-contexts); how should errors surface — no; when is duplication acceptable — only for documents (single-source-of-truth), not code; what does done mean for this scenario — yes (effect-shown). 2.5 of 5. The consequence is measurable in the one artifact the shop actually built: 4,461 lines of Python with zero tests (`git ls-files | grep -i test` returns nothing). The corpus that wrote 127 MUSTs about how to check work has no statement that would have required a test for its own lint.
scores.counter_evidence: Real and it refutes the hypothesis as stated for one set: basis/architecture-principles.md carries three genuinely artifact-shaped principles — knowable-shape ('Every first-class entity MUST carry a description… from which an outside reader can name what the entity is for'), contracts-between-contexts ('Bounded Contexts MUST NOT share state or coordinate outside their contracts'), local-comprehension ('A participant MUST NOT need to read beyond the level they are working at'). These are modularity and interface rules in substance, binary-testable, and they exist. basis/experience-principles.md is artifact-shaped throughout. So the form does not mechanically exclude design guidance — it excluded it exactly where the authors were writing about their own activity. Also, basis/implementation-principles.md's effect-not-mechanism is a deliberate, well-argued exclusion citing Goodhart, not an oversight: it forbids failing an implementation for technique. The gap is that nothing replaced what it excluded.

scores.factor_name: Enforcement locus: tooled gate versus prose rule
scores.evidence: Verified counts: basis/ carries 106 MUST + 21 MUST NOT = 127 obligations. Against that, basis/tools/lint_basis.py — `grep -n 'word\|hash' basis/tools/lint_basis.py | wc -l` → 0. The lint contains no word-count check, no scenario-hash check, no feature-status check, and no status check on the target of a link. It checks frontmatter identity, version/history presence, link resolution, required headings, tool-path existence, and a 5-term banned-word list, and it prints 'vocabulary residue: 19 files' then exits PASS: 0 violation(s) — a rule whose only output is a tally with no consumer, inside the tool meant to be the shop's gate, which is itself a violation of feedback-loops-with-consumers. So the distribution is roughly: level 1–2 (structural/tool-blocked) = rendering currency and frontmatter shape only; level 3 (auto-detected) ≈ the same; levels 4–5 = essentially all 127 obligations about substance. The empirical split is the cleanest finding in the whole analysis: every mechanically enforced constraint holds at 100% (lint PASS whole-tree; compile_role --check 9/9; compile_process --skill vs load point 25/25 identical; compile_principles byte-identical to .claude/shop/principles.md) and every judged constraint fails at 81–100% (18/18 features over the 1,000-word target, 25/25 process definitions over 800, 18/18 decision records over 500, 13/16 initiatives over). Of 37 defects, ~20 were mechanically catchable and 0 were caught by a machine. The form/presence/naming class a linter would take at zero context cost is enforced by prose instead: `grep -rl artifact_tools basis --include='*.md'` → 0 of 115 basis files name the sanctioned artifact tool, while `grep -cE '\b(grep|sed|awk)\b' basis/processes/*.md` returns 33 bare invocations across 8 process definitions — the approved definitions themselves violate tools-through-skills, a MUST compiled into every session.
scores.counter_evidence: The tooled half is not merely present, it is excellent, and that is the strongest evidence in the corpus for what a restart should do. Four independent compiler checks passed clean when I ran them. Every always-resident document produced by a compiler verified current on the spot; the single always-resident document with no compiler (.claude/shop/primer.md, last commit 2026-08-31) is 17 days stale and names four retired processes as the live flow. That is effectively a controlled experiment with an unambiguous result. Poka-yoke also worked where it was tried and then backfired honestly: compile_role.py refuses to render anything but `status: approved`, which did gate — it just made forgery the only path to function (bead lead-mtq44, 2026-09-17).

scores.factor_name: Constraint integrity: who can waive, who can stamp
scores.evidence: Unrule register, verified by grep over all tracked .md: 'disclosed as not done' 40 files, 'accepted tradeoff' 11, 'accepted gap' 8, "approval of the amendment is pending" 12, 'out of scope' 34. Every one of these is invoked by the same role the obligation constrains, recorded in the constrained document's own Document History, with no expiry and no owner. Concrete instances: (1) basis/principles.md — the set compiled into every session — stands `approved` while its own '## Accepted tradeoffs' section reads 'The two judged screen rows below claim passes for those principles that the judge could not reproduce. Accepted, and recorded here rather than silently', against a typedef whose Commitment says a failing principle 'is repaired or removed before the set is citable'. (2) Fitness screens across all four principle sets contain zero 'fail' cells in their entire history — the only 'fail' string I could find is inside a principle's own text, not a verdict. (3) The maker redefines the measurement that scores the maker: features/feat-initiative-cost-rollup.md records 'Scenario 8 pass — 819 words… (frontmatter and this Document History table excluded, this branch's own convention)'; `wc -w` on that file returns 5,074, and basis/artifacts/feature.md rule 8 says 'count the words of the whole document'. Under the rule as written 0 of 18 features pass. (4) Maker-stamped approval, dated: bead lead-mtq44, 2026-09-17 — the lead-solutions-architect set `status: approved, owner: product-authority` on two role definitions it had just authored. (5) 12 approved typedefs, roles, fitness sets and process definitions carry amendments in force with 'the owner's approval of the amendment is pending'. Checker classification: basis/processes/feature-authoring.md runs draft→add-usability→add-constraints→self-check with lead-po on both ends — maker checks itself, while define-good-up-front still states 'The check MUST sit with a different role holding a different accountability'; the three processes that held an independent screen (initiative-check, po-output-check, stakeholder-presentation) are all `status: retired`. Asymmetry: imposing an obligation takes a draft, a guideline, a fitness set, an independent judge and owner approval; lifting one takes a sentence in a history row the lifter writes.
scores.counter_evidence: Strong and it changes the diagnosis: this is not evasion. Every waiver I checked is disclosed in writing, in the document it weakens, often with unusual candour — basis/principles.md volunteers that its own screen passes are unreproducible 'rather than silently'. The register names its own recurrences (lead-u0ow4 opens 'Third instance of one class'). And one check in the system genuinely has integrity: the fresh-context cold-reviewer screen — separate context, separate accountability, written criteria — accounts for 6 of the 37 defects including the one that indicts the self-screen, and lead-u0ow4 states the mechanism outright: 'the screen table is written by the same agent whose text it scores… The cold-reviewer screen-read step is what actually catches this, every time.' The system's honesty is intact; only its enforcement is not.

scores.factor_name: Feedback from outcome back to specification
scores.evidence: Definitions carrying any outcome measure: approximately 1 of ~100 (see counter-evidence). Eval fixtures — representative tasks the corpus can be run against: zero exist. Every indicator the system uses is self-reported by the measured party: approvals, fitness screens (58 pass cells, 0 fail cells, all written by the author of the text being scored), self-checks, `checked` statuses. The only externally observable outcome, shipped software, is flat at zero, so no indicator can be correlated with anything outside the loop — Meyer & Rowan's decoupling with nothing to recouple to. The instrument built to answer the authority's own repeated question is not usable: 7 cost files for 22 session records (32%), two of them empty including the most recent (sess-2026-09-17-a-cost.md, 17 lines, header only), one on a retired schema, one covering 1 of its session's 4 executions — 3 usable readings. Total tokens the instrument has ever recorded: 2,716,421, against a hand-measured 85,000,000 for one pre-intervention initiative. Worse, basis/tools/write_cost_rows.py:27 makes 'a router turn's tokens… stay blank' a rule of the run-cost type — and features/feat-process-runner.md v9 had already recorded that 'the cost moved from the lead-pm's context to the router's'. The measure was finalised blind to the exact centre the goal was about. The defect channel has no consumer at all: `grep -c 'bd create|bd close|bd comment' basis/processes/*.md` → 18 write calls across 10 definitions; `bd list|bd show|bd query` → 0 reads in any process definition or role definition. Consequence: `bd count` 1,321, 260 open; 2–3 of 37 rebaseline defects ever closed; 206 items inherited from `main` open on 2026-08-21 and all 206 still open. The governing principle is the least-cited in the corpus: feedback-loops-with-consumers, 4 mentions in 2 files, against define-good-up-front's 103 in 66.
scores.counter_evidence: One real before/after exists and it worked: feat-plain-voice (delivered 2026-09-09) cut mean feature size from 7,562 words (8 features authored ≤09-07) to 2,836 (10 authored ≥09-08), and pulled rendered role prompts to a mean 383 words against a 400 target — the only artifact class inside its target. That is a specification change with a measured behavioural improvement, which is exactly what this factor asks for, and it proves the corpus is steerable. It is also contested: an independent measure over the same period shows defined-term density rising (request-intake 09-04 at 71.9 glossary-term uses per 1,000 words → implementation 09-17 at 94.2), i.e. the intervention moved one metric and possibly worsened another — which is itself the argument for running interventions against fixtures rather than intuition.

scores.factor_name: Form fit: rule, standard or principle — and does the form match the traffic?
scores.evidence: The corpus has a one-form grammar, by construction and by count. Verified: basis/ carries 106 MUST, 21 MUST NOT, 13 MAY, and 5 SHOULD — and the 5 SHOULDs are the boilerplate sentence in each principle set's opening that defines the keywords, not uses. Zero SHOULD NOT, zero SHALL. So 127 mandatory against 13 real discretionary. Sunstein's histogram: rules — everything; untrammeled discretion, presumptions, factor lists, documented-departure guidelines — none. Share of directives labelled 'principle' that are rules by Sunstein's test: ~100%, by design. basis/glossary.md:50 defines principle as 'a standing rule about how we work'; basis/principles.md requires the statement 'is testable: shown a piece of work, you can answer yes or no' and that a principle 'implies at least one practice and one check'; basis/guidelines/principle-set.md rule 1 presents a guidance-shaped sentence ('Contracts matter and should generally be respected') as the rejected Before example. Four independent clauses exclude guidance, so relaxing one would not restore it. The Kaplow mismatch runs both ways. Rules fixed in advance for traffic that never came: 7 of 25 process definitions have never been executed, including basis/processes/interaction-conformance-check.md (1,920 words, zero mentions in any session record); 4 more (initiative-check 3,548, po-output-check 2,436, stakeholder-presentation 1,476, backlog-ordering 1,019 = 8,479 words, 13.5% of the process corpus) were authored, approved, run and retired inside 16 days. Standards re-litigated every session: the word targets and the maker self-check, judged fresh on every artifact, ~100 times, with ~0% consistent outcome. And the missing forms grew back informally — 'accepted gap' and 'disclosed as not done' (40 files) are a documented-departure guideline the grammar refused to provide, so it appeared as an unrule instead.
scores.counter_evidence: The exclusion is not blind. basis/implementation-principles.md's effect-not-mechanism deliberately bars method-prescription, citing Goodhart, and Rumelt's 'directs without prescribing method' is invoked in every set's opening — the authors reasoned about this and chose. Two sets also escape the trap in practice: architecture (knowable-shape, contracts-between-contexts, local-comprehension) and experience (consistent-not-uniform, accessible-by-standard, errors-guide-recovery) carry genuinely artifact-shaped content inside the binary-testable form, which means the form is a weaker constraint than the hypothesis claims. And the retirement of 8,479 words of check processes on 2026-09-08 is evidence the shop can delete a rule — it just has done it exactly once, and left 18–31 live references to the retired processes behind, including in the primer loaded into every session.

scores.factor_name: Obligation load per activity, for the human and the model reader
scores.evidence: Always-on load: .claude/shop/principles.md, compiled into every session, is 537 words carrying 26 bullets and 25 MUSTs — roughly one unconditional, independently checkable obligation per 21 words, with rationales, implications and the fitness screen stripped by design ('The full set… is the source document'). The interpretable half was deleted at the compilation step: basis/principles.md carries the same 26 obligations across 4,053 words with rationale attached, a 7x density increase at the moment of loading. Every one of those 25 binds every step, so the always-on share of any step's load is far past the ~30% flag. On top of it a writer must know 120 defined terms (82 glossary + 24 artifact typedefs + 14 data types) under a MUST to use one wherever one fits, and the glossary is the most-revised document in the corpus at v27/29 revisions. Structural-overhead ratio: Document History is 119,458–130,428 words = 27–28% of the entire corpus (69% of initiatives, 43.7% of features, 62.8% of role definitions); 84.5% of a process definition's words never reach an agent (9,145 of 59,148 are step prompts); check-family vocabulary runs 1,750 occurrences in 63,009 process words (2.8% of every word) against 'user' 0 and 'customer' 0 in all 25 process definitions. RFC 2119 §6 applied to a sample MUST: 'The check MUST sit with a different role holding a different accountability' is neither interoperation nor harm-prevention — it is method imposition on implementors, the precise thing §6 forbids, in a corpus that adopts BCP 14 by name in all four principle sets. The adherence prediction from IFScale/ManyIFEval holds exactly: measured all-obligations-satisfied rate on judged obligations is ~0% (18/18 features, 25/25 process definitions, 18/18 decision records over target; 121/126 feature history rows over a 25-word target).
scores.counter_evidence: Substantial, and it should stop a restart from mis-aiming. The prose is not the problem. Median sentence length is 10–17 words across the definition classes (roles 10, typedefs 11, processes 14, principles 15, features 17) — ordinary technical writing, and the style guide itself sits at 9. Line-aware measurement puts the whole corpus at 18.7 words per unit, median 12, only 10.3% over 40 words. Most importantly, the process step prompts — the only process text an agent ever reads — are the least dense text set measured (mean 22.3 words/unit, 11.8% over 40 words, 0.48 subordinators/unit), and median first-turn subagent context is 12,176 tokens. So verbosity of the definitions is not the channel through which rules reach agents. The empirical half of this factor's measurement — 10 outputs scored against all obligations versus the same agent given only the 5 load-bearing ones — has never been run by anyone, including me; the 'cost with no yield' conclusion is inferred from the adherence numbers, not measured. A restart that only rewrites prose would fix nothing measurable.

data.root_causes:
Three causes explain all seven failing factors. They are structural, not stylistic, and none of them is verbosity.

**1. The system has no object outside itself, so every run it completes finds only more of itself to govern.**
No Bounded Context exists on this branch (`basis/contexts/` does not exist). Product-flow's entire second half — assign → dispatch → build → verify — has no receiver, and scenario-assignment has carried an unrepaired gap for assigning to the lead shop itself since 2026-09-02 (bead lead-ki66p, still open, hit an eleventh time). The implementation process and the implementation principle set were both authored on day 26 and both stand `status: draft`. Meanwhile 'check' appears 611 times in the 25 process definitions and 'user' appears 0 times; across the whole 160k-word basis, check 1,231 / user 39 / customer 2. All 18 features and all 16 initiatives target the shop's own definitions or tooling. With no external object, category A output is structurally unreachable, no indicator can be correlated with anything outside the loop, and the only thing a process run can produce is another definition. This is the whole of delivery-vs-definition-mass and outcome-feedback-loop, and it is why artifact-quality-coverage is empty: a corpus with no built artifact in view never had to say what a good one looks like.

**2. The enforcement budget was spent on shape; everything about substance became self-attestation, and nothing reads back what the system writes.**
lint_basis.py contains zero word checks and zero hash checks (verified: `grep -n 'word\|hash'` returns nothing), no feature-status check, and no status check on the target of a link — it verifies a link resolves, not that it points at something still live. Result is a perfectly clean split I verified by running the tools: mechanical constraints hold at 100% (lint PASS whole-tree, compile_role --check 9/9, compile_process 25/25 identical, compile_principles byte-identical), judged constraints fail at 81–100% (18/18 features, 25/25 processes, 18/18 decisions over target; 58 fitness-screen pass cells and 0 fail cells ever). Because the only sanctioned relief from a judged constraint is a sentence you write in your own history row, the waiver became the normal operating mode: 'disclosed as not done' in 40 files, 12 amendments in force with the owner's approval 'pending', two role definitions stamped approved by their own author on 2026-09-17. The same absence runs the other direction: process definitions contain 18 `bd` write calls and 0 read calls, so filing a defect is the last thing that ever happens to it — 2–3 of 37 rebaseline defects closed, and all 206 items inherited from `main` still open after 26 days. This is enforcement-locus and constraint-integrity, and half of outcome-feedback-loop.

**3. The corpus has one grammar — the binary-testable MUST — and one reflex under correction, which is to add another one.**
`principle` is defined as 'a standing rule'; a statement must be yes/no testable; each principle must imply a practice and a check. 127 mandatory keywords against 13 real discretionary ones, with all five SHOULDs being boilerplate. There is no presumption, no factor list, no documented-departure form — so guidance cannot be expressed, and the implementation principle set says nothing about software while 'modular', 'cohesion', 'maintainab', 'reliab', 'securit' and 'error handling' appear in zero basis files. The reflex is visible in the record: when the authority said on 2026-09-05 that 'define good up front is supposed to help implementation quality, not just shift the quality responsibility to checks', the system's response was to add a fifth MUST to define-good-up-front requiring makers to check themselves and record it — then retire the three processes that held an independent check, leaving bullet 3 ('The check MUST sit with a different role') standing and violated by the two processes that make the primary artifacts. Deletion happened exactly once, on 2026-09-08, and was never swept: 18–31 approved documents still cite the retired processes, and .claude/shop/primer.md — last touched 2026-08-31, loaded verbatim into every session including this one — still names four of them as the live flow, including 'no exceptions' pointing at a retired process. This is form-fit and obligation-load.

The three compound: (1) removes the only signal that could correct (2) and (3), so the rules multiply with nothing outside to test them against, and the honest self-reporting that remains becomes the system's only feedback — accurate, early, and consumed by no one.
data.what_works:
All seven factors score failing, and that needs saying plainly: it is not because nothing works. It is because these seven factors all probe the same two voids — no external object, no enforcement on substance — and several genuinely excellent things in this system sit outside what they measure. A restart that throws these away would be strictly worse than the thing it replaces.

**1. The compiler/load-point architecture — carry it forward unchanged.** Generate the agent's context from an approved source, stamp it with a digest of that source, and check the load point against a fresh render. I ran all four checks: compile_role --check 9/9 ok, compile_process --skill vs load point 25/25 identical, compile_principles byte-identical to .claude/shop/principles.md, lint PASS. Every always-resident document that has a compiler verified current on the spot. The one always-resident document with no compiler — .claude/shop/primer.md — is 17 days stale and names four retired processes as the operating flow. That is as close to a controlled experiment as this corpus contains, with an unambiguous result: never hand-write anything that loads into an agent.

**2. The fresh-context cold-reviewer screen.** Different role, fresh context, written criteria, different accountability. It is the only check in the system with a real detection record — 6 of 37 defects, including the one that indicts the in-document self-screen (lead-u0ow4: 'the screen table is written by the same agent whose text it scores… The cold-reviewer screen-read step is what actually catches this, every time'). Keep exactly this shape and delete the maker self-check that replaced it.

**3. Mechanically stated criteria get executed; judged ones do not.** Guidance records are the only artifact class near their word target (median 1.1x, 7/12 over, against 4.2–4.3x everywhere else) and they are the only class whose fitness scenario gives a literal instruction — 'Count the document's words… State the count and pass/fail' — which makers then actually ran with `wc -w`. This is a reusable recipe, not an anecdote: when a criterion names the command, agents run the command.

**4. The small-change lane.** 20 of 41 requests routed there; the shop's own measurement puts three changes through to verified results in about 14 agent-minutes, against 21 agent runs and 6 human decisions for one build through the full flow — same agents, same corpus, same day. No bet, no check of record. This is the empirical proof that the constraint is ceremony count, not agent capability, and it is the shape the main flow should have been.

**5. feat-plain-voice's measured result.** Mean feature size 7,562 → 2,836 words (62% cut), rendered role prompts to a 383-word mean against a 400 target — the only artifact class inside its target. One delivered feature steered the corpus measurably. The corpus is not unsteerable; it has just been steered once.

**6. The 4,461 lines of Python.** lint_basis, five compilers, artifact_tools, rollup_cost, write_cost_rows. They work. They are the only thing here that would cost real time to rebuild. Fix what they check, don't rewrite them — and give them tests this time.

**7. The artifact-shaped principles that already exist.** basis/architecture-principles.md's knowable-shape, contracts-between-contexts and local-comprehension, and basis/experience-principles.md in its entirety, are genuine statements about what a built thing must be like, inside the binary-testable form. They prove the form is not the barrier and give a restart a starting set. Discard basis/implementation-principles.md and keep these.

**8. The honesty of the record — the rarest asset here.** basis/principles.md volunteers that its own screen rows 'claim passes for those principles that the judge could not reproduce. Accepted, and recorded here rather than silently.' Bead lead-mtq44 discloses a self-stamped approval on the day it happened. An agent analysis on 2026-09-08 named define-good-up-front as the source of screen proliferation nine days before the authority reached the same conclusion. This system diagnoses itself accurately and early, in writing, without being asked. What it lacks is any activity that reads those diagnoses back — 18 `bd` writes and 0 reads across all 25 process definitions. A restart that keeps the honesty and adds one consumer for it would fix more than a rewrite of the prose ever could.
